dedupe_keys.name: utrecht netherlands will charging electric ambulances affect response times elaspy simulation

description: This case study tests whether an ambulance service could switch from diesel to electric vehicles without slowing responses, using the province of Utrecht in the Netherlands as the example. The authors built ELASPY, an open-source discrete event simulation in Python of the emergency response process, and published the study as an open-access article. The model replays historical incidents with different battery capacities and charger locations, and a simulation-based optimisation framework allocates chargers to stations and hospitals. Coverage is the Utrecht region; the software is publicly available with documentation so other regions can insert their own incident data. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: results depend on assumed vehicle ranges and charging speeds, and the authors note that prolonged power outages and calamities remain a risk that daily-operation results do not cover. The study found that with suitable battery capacity and charger placement an electric fleet can achieve response times comparable to diesel under expected operating conditions. Simulation uses: an example of discrete event simulation for design and retrofit decisions and energy-transport interdependency in emergency services. Related records: the ELASPY model itself (model-elaspy-p02682).
